topics.name: Polite words and requests (please, may I, could you, sorry, pardon)

questions.rule: An instruction (imperative) starts with the base verb: Speak clearly.
To tell how someone did an action, use an adverb: answered politely.
One person (a good speaker) takes a verb with -s in the simple present: listens.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: answer is a verb. To say how, use the adverb politely.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After Don't in an instruction, use the base verb: Don't talk.
An instruction begins with the base form of the verb: Speak politely.
How did the baby smile? Use the adverb: smiled happily.
A 'don't' instruction: Don't + base verb: Don't shout.
To ask for permission, use May I + base verb: May I come in?

chat: Who will give the welcome speech?
questions.rule: will never takes -s or -ing. A short answer: I will, ma'am.

options: Shall I share my idea with the group, sir?
Shall I shares my idea with the group, sir?
Shall I sharing my idea with the group, sir?
questions.rule: After Shall I, use the base verb: Shall I share?
A negative instruction is Don't + base verb: Don't mumble.
How should you listen? Use the adverb: listen carefully.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A good speaker is one person, so the present verb takes -s: looks.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: may is followed by the base verb: may I borrow?
To ask for permission politely, we say May I + base verb: May I open?

questions.after: her speech in her mind first.
questions.rule: A habit is in the simple present. Riya is one person, so add -s: rehearses.
A polite request: Could you please + base verb?

chat: Can you hear me at the back?
questions.rule: An instruction uses the base verb speak. To tell how, use the adverb loudly.

chat: Here is my notebook for your speech notes.
questions.rule: The polite phrase is Thank you (or Thanks). We say so much, not so many.

options: Shy children often speaks very softly.
Shy children often speak very softly.
Shy children often speaking very softly.
questions.rule: children is plural, so the present verb has no -s: children speak. Speaking needs a helper verb.

options: Could you please passes me the microphone?
Could you please pass me the microphone?
Could you please passing me the microphone?
questions.rule: Could you please is followed by the base verb: pass.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: careful is an adjective. To tell how he listened, use the adverb carefully.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Many shy children is plural, so the present verb has no -s: feel.

questions.after: interrupt others when they are speaking.
questions.rule: A negative instruction uses Don't + base verb: Don't interrupt.
How did Raj answer? Use the adverb: answered wisely.
An instruction starts with the base verb: Let others share.
Thank you for + the thing you are thankful for.

options: No, ma'am. Could you explains it again, please?
No, ma'am. Could you explained it again, please?
No, ma'am. Could you explain it again, please?
questions.rule: After Could you, use the base verb: could you explain.

chat: How did you feel on the stage?
options: I feeled nervous, but I spoke clearly.
I felt nervous, but I speaked clearly.
I felt nervous, but I spoke clearly.
questions.rule: did asks about the past. Past of feel = felt, past of speak = spoke.

options: Yesterday, Meena gave her speech confidently.
Yesterday, Meena give her speech confidently.
Yesterday, Meena gave her speech confident.
questions.rule: Yesterday needs the past: gave. To tell how, use the adverb confidently.

options: Look at they when you talk to them.
Look at them when you talk to them.
Look at them when you talks to them.
questions.rule: After at use the object pronoun them. With you, the verb has no -s: you talk.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Last week is the past. The past of speak is spoke.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a preposition (to) use the object pronoun: to me, not to I.
After Thank you for, use the -ing form of the verb: thank you for helping.

questions.after: you get nervous before a speech?
questions.rule: A simple present question with you starts with Do + base verb.
A past question: Did + you + base verb (plan)?
I am sorry to + base verb is a polite way to interrupt someone.

chat: You keep talking all the time in our group!
options: I'm sorry. I will let others speak.
I'm sorry. I will lets others speak.
I'm sorry. I will let others speaks.
questions.rule: After will use the base verb (let), and after let others also the base verb (speak).

chat: What does Sana do before a speech?
questions.rule: Sana is one person, so the present verb takes -s: she notes down.

options: Neha spoke too fastly, so nobody understood her.
Neha spoke too fast, so nobody understood her.
Neha spoke too fast, so nobody understand her.
questions.rule: fast is already an adverb (no -ly). Both verbs are past: spoke, understood.

options: When you disagree, says it politely and give your reason.
When you disagree, say it polite and give your reason.
When you disagree, say it politely and give your reason.
questions.rule: Advice uses the base verb (say, give). To tell how, use the adverb politely.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The sentence is in the past (stood), so the past of forget is forgot.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: good is an adjective. The adverb that tells how you rehearse is well.
Before a noun (voice) we need an adjective: a pleasant voice.

questions.before: If you do not understand something,
questions.rule: This is advice to you, so use the instruction form, the base verb: ask.
Pardon me + could you + base verb is a polite way to ask someone to repeat.

chat: Let's hold the class party on Friday.
options: Sorry, but I doesn't agree. Saturday is better for all of us.
Sorry, but I don't agree. Saturday is more better for all of us.
Sorry, but I don't agree. Saturday is better for all of us.
questions.rule: With I say don't. good - better: never more better.

chat: Why are you practising your speech again?
options: Because I wants to speak well tomorrow.
Because I want to speak good tomorrow.
Because I want to speak well tomorrow.
questions.rule: With I, no -s: I want. To tell how you speak, use the adverb well.

chat: Shall we make the poster bigger?
options: Yes, that is a great idea. Let's doing it.
Yes, that is a great idea. Let's does it.
Yes, that is a great idea. Let's do it.
questions.rule: Let's is followed by the base verb: Let's do it.
